newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TVB cautious on outlook for second half.
newsitem.headline: TVB cautious on outlook for second half.

text.p: Hong Kong's biggest media group, Television Broadcasts Ltd (TVB), gave a cautious outlook for its business in Hong Kong in the second half of 1996 after reporting on Thursday interim results that were below expectations.
However, the broadcaster was more sanguine on the outlook for its smaller international operations.
TVB announced a 5.8 percent decline in earnings to HK$177.96 million in first half 1996, compared with HK$189.01 million a year earlier.
The results were significantly below expectations. Analysts had been expecting to see interim earnings growth roughly in line with full year forecasts of 20 percent.
One analyst said turnover had risen by 11.5 percent to HK$1.33 billion, thus indicating a squeeze in profit margins. But he could give no reason for the decline in profitability.
The company said it had enjoyed a sustained high audience share compared to the previous period and increasing awareness and appreciation of its programming in international markets.
However, growth was constrained by a sluggish local economy and a depressed advertising market which resulted in a marginal reduction in interim profits.

Looking forward, the report said the company saw early signs of recovery in the Hong Kong economy, but said the impact on TVB's operations in 1996 would be modest. Further improvement in 1997 was anticipated, it said.
The report pointed to the company's Taiwan operations where its cable TV channel TVBS achieved profitability within two years of launch and had a bright future, the report said.
It said other projects still in their early stages augured well for the company's expanding international business activities. It gave no further details.
